title: Outreach is queued to a local outbox, not delivered — no real provider integration; sourced candidates are name-addressed and would dead-letter even with a relay
expected: Firing 'Reach out' delivers a first-touch email/SMS to the candidate via a real provider, or the UI states plainly that it only queued locally.
got: dispatchOutreach → sendComm → OutboxChannel records status 'queued', which the code itself calls 'a terminal dev state: the outbox IS the delivery target'. A real path exists only as a generic COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL webhook (no SendGrid/SES/Twilio in-repo). Recipient for sourced/rediscovered candidates resolves to a human NAME (never an email — 'the data model stores none'), which the contract says a relay 'cannot deliver to … will dead-letter'. The UI announces 'a first-touch message is on its way'.
scope_note: The outbox-by-default architecture is documented (docs/COMMS_DELIVERY.md) and the Comms Center discloses it in-product (relay banner, deliverable:false warnings, dead-letter chase) — that honesty keeps this major, not blocker.
l2_priority: Fire one outreach live; open Channels → Comms Center and confirm the row is status 'queued' with a bare-name recipient, and that the relay banner / deliverability warning states the truth on this fixture.
suggested_acceptance: Either a first-class provider channel (email at minimum) behind the existing CommsChannel seam with address capture for sourced candidates, or the reach-out confirmation copy changed to say 'queued to the outbox' when no relay is configured.

title: Outreach draft prompt grounding 4/8 — no ČS brand/tone, no role depth, no candidate-profile depth, and no awareness the candidate is a rediscovered silver medalist
expected: A first-touch draft grounded in the full role (team, stack, location, band), the candidate's real trajectory, ČS's employer voice — and, for a rediscovered candidate, the prior relationship ('you reached our final round for X').
got: The prompt receives exactly: candidate label, job.title + job.company, up to a few matched skills, and the output language. A silver medalist gets cold-contact copy ('your background caught our eye' — false for someone who was in the process before). Reaches the prompt: name ✓, matched strengths ✓, title+company ✓, language ✓; role depth ✗, brand kit ✗, prior-relationship context ✗, profile depth ✗.
l2_priority: Generate a live draft for a Czech rediscovered candidate and judge it against Jana's send-bar: on-brand, human, specific, no obvious-AI tells, and not tone-deaf to the prior relationship.
suggested_acceptance: Prompt receives the prior-outcome context (pickPrior already computes it), the job's team/stack/location facts, and a short ČS tone directive; a rediscovered candidate's draft must reference the prior relationship.

title: The rediscovery WHY-NOW is a per-kind stock template (3 fixed sentences), not this candidate's fit-delta story
expected: Each rediscovered candidate carries a why-now derived from real fit deltas — what was missing then, why this role fits now (Jana's scored criterion; journey definition-of-done: 'not a bare re-score').
got: The why-now line is t('whyNow.<prior.kind>') — one of exactly three localized templates keyed rejected/closed/elsewhere, interpolating only jobTitle + score. It IS grounded in the real prior outcome and the real deterministic score (better than a bare name), but the candidate-specific delta (matchedSkills / missing skills are present in the ranked payload rows) is dropped before the why-now is rendered — a dressed-up re-score.
l2_priority: Run rediscovery on a role with ≥3 silver medalists and read the rows side by side: do the why-now lines visibly repeat the same 3 sentences?
suggested_acceptance: Why-now composed from the candidate's ranked-row detail (top matched skills for THIS role, the requirement that sank them last time if derivable) rather than a kind-keyed template.

title: Reach out fails with 404 'job not found' for any in-app-created role — the outreach draft resolves the job from the static seed corpus, not the DB
expected: The outreach draft uses the authoritative server-side job record (the journey file assumes route.ts:43-51's trust posture extends to the draft).
got: The pipeline ENTRY gets the server job record, but the DRAFT's job comes from Python: automation-run.ts passes only --job-id for outreach (no --jobs), automation_cli loads load_corpus(None) = data/seed_jobs/jobs.normalized.json and raises NotFoundError for an unknown id. In-app ingested/published roles exist only in SQLite (jobs table) → Reach out 404s on them; an in-app-EDITED seed role drafts from stale seed facts. The TS comment 'Other tasks score a single job and skip the corpus entirely' is wrong — they resolve the job FROM the corpus (the same gap idea-e01935e9 fixed for rematch only).
l2_priority: Ingest + publish a fresh role in-app, open its candidates/rediscover tab, click Reach out → expect the 404 'job not found' error surfaced on the button.
suggested_acceptance: Outreach (and screen/rejection/prep/scorecard/offer) receive the live DB job via --job-json, mirroring rankPoolForJob and the campaign route.

title: Analysis-sourced pool candidates can be ranked and rediscovered but NOT reached out — 400 'candidate profile not found', and the failed attempt still silently files them into the pipeline
expected: Any candidate the pool ranks and rediscovery surfaces can be outreached; a failed outreach leaves no half-handled state.
got: buildCandidatePool includes saved CV analyses (id = analysis slug) alongside v2 profiles, so rediscovery surfaces them — but runAutomationTask resolves the candidate via getProfileRecord only (profiles table; loadAnalysis is never consulted, unlike resolveCandidatePoolEntry which falls back). Result: AutomationError 400. Compounding: createPipelineEntry runs BEFORE the draft, so the errored candidate is filed at Screened anyway — which removes them from the rediscover list on next load (hist jobId===job.id && active filter), leaving them looking 'handled' with no first touch sent.
l2_priority: Reach out on an analysis-sourced rediscovered candidate → expect the 400 error on the row AND the candidate appearing on the pipeline board at Screened with no outreach_sent event.
suggested_acceptance: runAutomationTask falls back to the analysis payload (poolEntryFromAnalysis path) when no profile row exists, or the outreach route resolves via resolveCandidatePoolEntry before filing the entry.

title: Pool caps (100 profiles + 60 analyses) silently bound who can ever be rediscovered — overflow is a server-console warning only
expected: Rediscovery's promise is 'strong past candidates never fall through the cracks'; if the scanned population is truncated, the recruiter is told in the UI.
got: buildCandidatePool caps at PROFILE_POOL_CAP=100 + ANALYSIS_POOL_CAP=60; when hit, older candidates are excluded from ranking AND rediscovery with only a console.warn. On the current seed fixture the caps likely aren't hit (frequency low today) — at ČS scale (thousands of past applicants) the core promise silently breaks, with zero UI signal.
l2_priority: Optional: seed >100 profiles and confirm the rediscover panel gives no truncation hint.
suggested_acceptance: When a cap is hit, the /rediscover and /candidates payloads carry a truncation flag the panels render (mirroring the existing 'more' count pattern in rediscover.ts:97-102).

title: Prior-outcome chips render hardcoded English ('Rejected · …', 'Closed · …', stage names) inside the Czech UI on both rediscovery surfaces
expected: Jana's language criterion: UI renders correctly in Czech.
got: pickPrior builds English literal labels (`Rejected · ${role}`, `Closed · ${role}`, `${stage} · ${role}`) that RediscoverPanel and RediscoveryFeed render verbatim; the RediscoverPanel comment itself calls it 'the legacy English prior.label' (the why-now line was localized, the chip wasn't).
l2_priority: Confirm the mixed-language chip renders in the cs locale.
suggested_acceptance: Ship prior.kind + structured fields (role, stage) on the wire and localize the label at the render site, like whyNow already does.

title: The standing rediscovery feed is inert on the seeded ČS fixture — sweep and relevance cover only status='published' roles, and seeded corpus rows are status NULL
expected: The feed surfaces silver-medalist hits for the roles the recruiter is actually working — on this fixture, the seeded ČS corpus.
got: sweepRediscoveryAlerts iterates listJobStatuses() filtered to 'published' (only non-NULL statuses exist there), and relevantAlerts applies the same filter at read time; seeded corpus jobs carry status NULL ('NULL = seeded/live corpus job'). On the bare fixture every sweep reports 0 roles and the feed never fires until a role is published in-app. The feed's note is at least honest ('no published roles').
ceiling: Even once a role is published, the feed only knows publish-time + manual-sweep snapshots — there is no background trigger on pool change.
scope_note: Arguably correct semantics (alert only on live openings); the finding is the fixture/expectation mismatch — a recruiter on the seeded corpus sees a permanently empty feed with no path to make it useful.
l2_priority: Click Refresh on the seeded fixture → expect 'swept 0 roles'; then publish one role and confirm alerts appear.
suggested_acceptance: Either treat status-NULL corpus roles as sweepable, or have the empty state explain 'publish a role to activate rediscovery alerts'.

title: Once-only, consent-gated outreach: durable outreach_sent gate + in-process single-flight + audited consent suppression + idempotent filing
got: A cache-HIT re-click cannot double-send (durable marker checked before dispatch, in-flight set released on failure so retries work); expired-consent/anonymized candidates are suppressed with an audit event and NO marker so re-consent stays contactable; createPipelineEntry is idempotent.
l2_priority: Double-click Reach out live and confirm exactly one outbox row.

title: Unscorable candidates are surfaced, never silently dropped — the skipped note rides above results even when the rediscovery list is empty
got: The rediscover route threads `skipped` through explicitly ('rediscovery … never silently drops them'), and the panel renders the note before the empty state — a malformed profile may be exactly why the list looks empty.

title: The ranked pool answers 'found them HOW?' — per-skill provenance badges, confidence bands with drivers, assumptions, KO reasons with near-miss flags, and a cross-scheme fairness audit with CSV export
got: Exactly Jana's anti-black-box requirement: every matched skill carries a provenance chip, not-eligible candidates expose their KO reasons sorted near-miss-first, and Fair Rank exposes own-vs-robust scoring with an exportable per-scheme matrix.

title: Sourcing state persists across sessions — ranked rows are server-decorated with inPipeline stage and outreachSent, so a reopened role shows reality, not fresh buttons
got: W8-5: the durable truth (entries keyed jobId+candidateId, per-entry outreach_sent event) decorates each ranked row; a reached candidate collapses to a single badge, an already-filed one shows its stage instead of a no-op add button.
l2_priority: Reload the role after a reach-out and confirm the badge state survives.

title: Campaign pack honesty contract — stated-facts-only with phantom filtering, warning codes for missing facts, AI-vs-deterministic provenance label, and per-variant attributed apply links
got: Fields normalize_job merely assumed (defaulted_fields) are treated as ABSENT so an anchor salary is never advertised as fact; missing facts surface as localized warnings; the pack states whether the LLM or the rule-based builder produced it; every variant's apply URL carries a variant id for creative attribution.

title: Comms Center deliverability honesty — relay-not-configured banner, unaddressable-recipient warnings, bounce/dead-letter chase and resend
got: The outbox audit surface distinguishes queued/sent/failed/bounced, warns when a recipient could never be delivered to by a real relay, and marks recovered dead-letters as audit rather than alarms — the build names its own seams (this is also what keeps SR-L1-001 major instead of blocker).
